seo_title: Win with AI, or Lose to It? with Ola and Justin Bebis
meta_description: A Thanksgiving special on winning with AI: Ola on his AI workflow, agents, Vano and his MetaMask rebuild, then Justin Bebis on the AI bubble, the Anthropic IPO and pump.fun's block zero fee.
summary: A Thanksgiving special. The hosts open on what they are thankful for, how to tell whether AI is really making you productive, and a week of near daily hacks. In Young Crypto Voices, Ola explains how he went all in on AI, his workflow from notes to Claude Code, how he keeps his AI agents safe, his market analyst Vano, his MetaMask rebuild and how to make money with AI. Then Justin Bebis joins on Thanksgiving to talk launch timing, whether the AI bubble has popped, the Anthropic IPO, pump.fun's block zero fee and why Mosh builds for deployers.
takeaways: The hosts argue that AI productivity should be judged by tangible outputs, not by hours spent chatting with a model. R2D2 shares how he tracked his own build journey day by day, including the days lost in frustrating loops, and says building the CR2 website himself showed him how much opportunity AI can unlock for non-technical people.

Ola's advice for beginners is to start with Claude and use it every day. His workflow: give each AI agent its own identity, capture ideas in notes, refine them until they no longer read like AI, then build in Claude Code. When he hits a wall, he sends screenshots and videos of what he means. His agents can work across his accounts, but never click a link without showing him first.

Ola demoed Vano, an AI market analyst you can ask about any asset, which tracks a watchlist, sends a daily summary and asks before it acts. His formula for making money with AI is to find a problem, narrow down who needs the fix and sell it as a service priced for the value it gives. To stand out, he rebuilt MetaMask's app with AI as an unofficial concept, which brought teams to his DMs.

Justin does not think the AI bubble has popped. He sees AI narrative trades and crypto fighting over the same dollar, and expects a slow exit of liquidity rather than a dramatic crash, with traditional markets better able to absorb the damage than crypto. He would rather own Anthropic common stock than OpenAI preferred stock, and thinks OpenAI now has to rush toward an IPO.

Justin calls pump.fun's block zero fee a positive change that will not do much on its own. He argues that when anyone can build an everything app, the winner shapes its product around one user, and that Mosh is building for token deployers while everyone else fights over traders. The hosts and Justin debate the ethics of the trenches and whether call-outs reward the wrong behaviour.
